failed_attempt_policy: No invented answer scores; each failed attempt contributes zero in the failure-aware condition metric.
timestamp_basis: Original creation time (filesystem birthtime) of each completed assessment file, using the user-approved file-creation-time convention. ISO8601 America/New_York, microsecond precision exposed by filesystem API.
blinding: Scores finalized without condition labels, selected strategies, aggregate results, raw traces or prior-run grades. Root used programmatic raw binding validation without displaying conditions. Answer style can reveal a strategy.
primary_metric: Mean correctness (0, 0.5 or 1) across all 45 attempts per condition, including 19 observed failures as zero. Percentages are mean rubric scores, not proportions fully correct.
interpretation: Cascade scores 0.9000 versus Vector 0.7778: a positive AI-graded development signal. The paired 15-question bootstrap difference is +0.1222, CI95 [0.0333, 0.2333].
Cascade has higher mean estimated cost and elapsed time than Vector (about 2.55 times cost and 1.49 times elapsed time); the corresponding paired cost and elapsed-time intervals include zero.

Cascade and reserved-selection Agentic both have an observed failure-aware mean of 0.9000. Their quality-difference interval is [-0.1667, 0.1333], so equivalence is not established. Cascade has lower measured elapsed time and lower known estimated-cost subtotal; one reserved-selection attempt has unknown cost.
This review does not establish the original joint claim of higher correctness, lower cost and lower latency against all fixed strategies.
limitations: Single AI evaluation workflow with delegated source checks and root adjudication; no independent human review or inter-rater reliability estimate.
15 development questions from one pinned repository, not 206 independent questions; no held-out evaluation has run.
Condition labels were examined only after the score freeze; answer style may nevertheless suggest a strategy.
Estimated costs are usage/price-schedule estimates, not bills; two attempted jobs have unknown cost. Elapsed time includes pacing waits.
Bootstrap intervals are descriptive development-set intervals without multiplicity adjustment.
The earlier run used a different shared prompt and human ratings. Cross-run differences cannot isolate redesign effects; do not pool the studies.
